articles.title: The INSIDER daily digest -- November 17, 2026
articles.description: This Tuesday INSIDER Daily Digest has news on Senate appropriators' defense spending legislation, plus the Defense and Commerce departments' launching a review of additive manufacturing adoption barriers and more. We start off with coverage of the Senate Appropriations Committee's fiscal year 2027 defense spending bill: Senate GOP defense bill reshuffles Pentagon priorities, with shipbuilding and R&D among the biggest bill-payers The Senate Appropriations Committee's Republican majority is proposing a major reshuffling of the Pentagon's budget, steering billions of dollars toward missiles, munitions and other weapons priorities while reducing funding for shipbuilding, research and development as well as military operations. Senate Republicans shift $69B in defense reconciliation funding to regular appropriations Senate Republicans are proposing to move nearly $69 billion in defense funding sought by the Trump administration through budget reconciliation into the regular appropriations process as part of a nearly $1.1 trillion fiscal year 2027 defense spending bill that makes major investments in munitions production, missile defense, drones, shipbuilding and military modernization. Senate appropriators would add $25.8B into base budget for Army missile procurement Senate appropriators' version of the fiscal year 2027 defense spending bill would add $25.8 billion into the base budget for Army missile procurement, which would essentially shift those dollars from the Trump administration's originally proposed $350 billion reconciliation package. Document: Senate appropriators' draft FY-27 defense spending bill The Defense and Commerce departments want to "identify and dismantle the qualification cost and timeline barriers hindering the scaling of additive manufacturing across the defense industrial base": DOD and Commerce launch review of additive manufacturing adoption barriers The Defense Department is working with a Commerce Department office to conduct a nationwide review of barriers to verifying and adopting additive manufacturing processes across the defense industrial base. The effort comes as the military services increasingly look to adopt the technology, raising questions about whether existing verification and approval processes could slow its broader use. The Pentagon has released its Fiscal Year 2026 Agency Financial Report, "reflecting a new centralized approach in financial management and employing Super Intelligence (SI) to end wasteful processes and solve financial vulnerabilities": Pentagon touts audit progress under new strategy amid 9th failure; GAO has warned of risks The Defense Department, following its ninth consecutive department-wide audit failure, has announced significant progress in its effort to achieve a clean, department-wide opinion, projecting that clean opinions will cover more than 56% of its assets and more than 90% of its liabilities by February 2027. Document: DOD's FY-27 agency financial report The first 14 T-7 Red Hawk training aircraft haven't all been delivered yet: T-7 program could miss 2027 IOC goal The Air Force's T-7A Red Hawk trainer is at "risk" of slipping past its fall 2027 initial operational capability timeline, the head of Air Education and Training Command said this week, potentially delaying the already troubled program even further. An Army accelerated capability event, held this month in partnership with United States Army Pacific, featured an evaluation of "mature" unmanned ground systems built to solve the "contested last mile logistics" problem: Army G-TEAD to award up to six OTAs for unmanned ground systems following Hawaii event The Army's Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate (G-TEAD) plans to award as many as six other transaction agreements following an accelerated capability event (ACE) conducted this month in Hawaii, officials told reporters Friday.
